entry.title: Secrets of the Frontier 0.15.2
entry.content:
Secrets of the Frontier went from 0.15.1 to 0.15.2.
- New Cult of the Daydream ship: Rose-class interdictor - An elite destroyer specializing in bombarding, controlling and erasing hostiles from afar - Spite is the armor of beauty, make the enemy suffer! - Obtained similarly to other CotD designs; loading a Child of the Lake save will automatically add Rose-class to known blueprints - New Dustkeeper flagships: Doxology-class heavy frigate and Polychronios-class & Anapausis-class cruisers - Doxology: an overengineered teleporting menace with too many guns - Polychronios: a disruptive support ship with an EWAR focus - Anapausis: a time-accelerated hunter-killer rewarding strategic use of its charged system - All 3 are used as the leader of smaller Dustkeeper fleets - You can order these from Inadvertent when he has spare forge slots and you have enough reputation with him - Also, one guaranteed recoverable derelict of each will appear in high-danger Remnant systems
- Added Thrice-Speared "support" category traits. These can only spawn once you reach level 10 and have a decent-sized (120DP) fleet, and have wide-reaching effects - New Thrice-Speared traits: - Decaying Scourge (offense): Can periodically lash a nearby ship, dealing 8% of its current hull value as damage over time. Also halts the target. Versus nanite mimics and reflections, also overloads for 2s and deals an additional 8% of current hull instantly - Elegy of Opis (support): Gain a charge for each dead ally ship, at 3 charges the next ally that would be destroyed instead enters an undying rage, regaining 35% hull but decaying over time - Hands of the Drowned (support): Passively spawns waves of gravitic mines that deal damage and pull in their victims - reality_breaker (support): NullPointerException (KILL IT KILL IT KILL IT) - The Perfect Storm (support): Every 50 seconds, overloads ALL player-side ships for 3 seconds unless they are venting or phased (non-player ships will try to use this to dodge the overload)
- Changes to anti-ship cannon strikes (i.e. Leviathan's Bane & some add-on mod ASCs): - Targets should react more naturally to the incoming attack (thanks zoeythegirlgal for the original code!) - Ships will now start turning around during the lockon sequence if they have front shields - Replaced lock-on rings with a text display and targeting indicator on affected ships (LIDAR beam is also still present). The text display is visible near the center of the screen if the target is the player's ship and they're panned away - Added a UI message when a player-side ship is targeted by an anti-ship cannon
- Concord - Soulbond: reduced OP cost from 10/15 des/cru to 8/12 - New Pledge sprite by Kirbo (thanks so much!!!!) - New Sierra conversation topics: Sirius, Oneslaught, Threat, Third Strike, Dweller
- New Respite sprite by Selkie and Snazzy (THANKS :)!!!) - Fixed Cyberwarfare Suite cooldown reduction and penetration stats being affected by each other's modifiers resulting in a net near-zero change - Cyberwarfare Suite cooldown reduction listed value nerfed (25% > 15%), actual effect buffed (2.5% > 15%) - Wendigo and Courser infex changed from Annex to "Infix" to denote their special status as hunter-killers - Mia's Star: Increased distance from core, trace volatiles to Hallowhall (this is partly a nerf - can no longer use soil nanites) - Rigging-Echo-Inadvertent is now added as a contact when met so he appears in the intel tab. Dustkeeper contacts (ie just him right now) don't count towards the player's max contacts - Dustkeeper fleet flagships are now more likely to be recoverable after battle with their fleets or burnouts - Wendigo's Ether Wolves fleet is now bigger - Added 2 new generic Dustkeeper portraits, Indigo and Orange. Yellow recruitable sliver is now orange on new saves - Increased priority of Dustkeeper Burnout comm dialogue so they're less likely to be overriden - Can now ask Cerulean Faithful to fix your Tri-Tachyon reputation
- Felcesis is now primarily referred to as "The Thrice-Speared" - Thrice-Speared: rebalanced earlygame difficulty rampup (now 1 trait until player has 40dp of ships, fewer daydream skills until 60dp, 2 traits until 100dp) - Thrice-Speared: invasion UI is now Sirius-flavored while playing Child of the Lake - Rebalanced support traits that were in the files but didn't appear normally. Added a toggle to replace the reality_breaker crashcode with an equivalent non-crash punishment - Dear Dotty: can no longer be rolled as a trait until player is level 5 - Revenant Host: replaced Wolves and Wardens with approximately equivalent DP of Thorns - The Haunted: added unique music to the ending dialogue sequence
- Polarized Nanorepair skill: now soft-caps the regen at 450/850/1250/1650 armor (e.g 1650 armor capital regens armor at rate of 1%/s, 3300 capital regens 0.5%/s). With Tahlan Shipworks, halved regen rate on ships with Hel Plating or Hel Carapace (sorry. Or you're welcome. It depends on if you play more CotL or Haunted, really) - Thorn: increased Hypnagogic Incursion flux dissipation boost (+100% base, decaying > +200% base, decaying) - Daydream Systems Engineering: now provides immunity to solar coronae and similar hazards, ala s-modded Solar Shielding - Mercy Multilance (beams and bolts): Reduced range (1000 > 700). TLDR for below changes: nerfed performance against armor and small ships - Mercy Multilance (beams): Now fires 5 beams (was 4) with increased spread. Total damage unchanged, effective armor penetration nerf. Increased base armor shred, reduced stacking (40 + 20 per extra multilance > 50 + 10). Fixed bug where the last stack of armor shred would never expire - Mercy Multilance (bolts): Now fires 24 bolts for total of 2400 fragmentation damage (was 12 bolts for 600 energy). No longer applies EMP damage (was 600). Slightly widened bolt spread - Chalice Resonance Cage: Increased flux per shot (1500 > 2250, flux efficiency including bolts ~0.77 > 1.15) - Daydream drone replicators: reduced max drones active (6 > 4), barb mount is still 2 - Drones fired using the system of Random Assortment of Things' Gilgamesh now self-destruct after 15 seconds (sorry)

entry.title: The Abyssal War 0.9.2
entry.content:
The Abyssal War went from 0.9.0 to 0.9.2.
Saves: Saves from 0.9 carry on: fleets already flying get their fabricators on first load.
swarm doctrine - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8
Download
AbyssalWar-0.9.2.zip
Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. It extracts to mods/ThreatIncursion - overwrite your existing folder rather than keeping both. Saves from 0.8 and 0.9 carry on; removing the mod mid-war breaks the save.
What it is The Threat (vanilla's abyssal fabricator swarm) colonises the fringe of the sector, grows, and invades the core worlds Its colonies are real markets with a real economy. You beat it by starving, bombing and invading them, not by killing fleets The NPC factions fight it on their own. You run your own colonies' war from one intel screen (The Abyssal War) Standalone. LunaLib optional. Nexerelin compatible. Safe to add mid-save
How a game goes At game start a hidden fringe system is seeded with several Threat colonies ("hives"). Nobody knows They grow, spread to neighbouring systems and scout the core. When they can afford a strike that beats what they saw, they attack A faction whose world is struck mobilises: war economy, patrols, scouts, one big attack fleet. Factions find hives only by flying into their systems You find hives the same way: fly into the system, or own a colony next door. Found hives appear on the board; the map hides the rest Once you have colonies, press Mobilise on the board. Your colonies bank hulls, marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies, and you spend them on orders A hive dies when its strata (below) reach zero: bomb it from orbit, land marines, or cut off what feeds it. Kill every hive and the war ends The core holds for years on its own and usually loses without you
The Threat, explained Strata is a hive's one number. It is the colony's ground defence, its hit points and its troops at once. Fight it on the ground or bomb it from orbit, and the number goes down. Below each size's threshold the colony drops a size; at zero it is destroyed Each size needs twice the strata of the last, so a size 8 hive is a fortress and a size 2 seed is nothing Strata is also its fleets. A hive has no standing garrison. When attacked, or to strike, it turns strata into ships ("budding"); when the ships come home it turns them back into strata ("absorbing"). A hive that buds a defence fleet has that much less on the ground Reclaimed hulls. The swarm consumes and repurposes the fleets it destroys. Each hive world keeps a count of the hulls it has taken; a fleet budded there includes those hulls, with Threat weapons, beside its own ships. A wreck also adds strata to the world The Fabrication Core is the industry that makes strata. It needs metals and fuel, more of each the bigger the colony. Both met in full: the hive grows a size at a time. Short: it holds. Starved: it loses strata daily and shrinks a size at a time until it is gone Hives import from each other like any market. Blockade a hive (hold its orbit with warships) and it imports nothing; only its own mines, refineries and fuel plants still feed its Core. Saturation bombardment disrupts those for a year A hive's accessibility is how much strata stands nearby ("swarm density"). Dense systems grow; an isolated hive starves Hives move strata between systems: back-line worlds bud fleets that fly to the front and are absorbed there. A world under attack pulls strata in. The hive's best mine, refinery and fuel plant never give strata away below their own size A strike is strata too. The hive stages strata at its front worlds, grows them toward size 8, then buds the mass as one strike sized to beat the defence its scouts saw Over your world the strike's ships break up into troops and land. Landed strata never come home Occupation. The swarm never takes a human world. Each district its army holds lets it eat one industry: the industry stops working, is consumed over its build time and is removed. What it eats becomes strata: troops while the fight is on, then Infestation Swarms in orbit once every district is held. With nothing left to eat the army lifts off and looks for the next world
Hulls consumed by the swarm
A hive's Core fed in full: metals 3 of 3, fuel 1 of 1, 600 strata a month, the next size in 36 days.
The same hive blockaded: nothing docks, the Core gets nothing, it loses a size in 24 days.
Killing a hive Find it: fly into the system. The Threat tab lists every found system nearest first, with what your last scout saw there and how old that is. Scout sends a scout from the board; Map shows the system Starve it: blockade the orbit, saturation-bomb its mine, refinery or fuel plant, or kill the hive those imports come from. A seed hive dies on blockade alone Bomb it: tactical bombardment from the dock razes strata for fuel. The hive buds ships from its strata to stop you; beat them first Invade it: Ground operations at the dock lands all or half your marines with heavy armaments. The front fights the strata standing and keeps fighting after you leave; Push or Hold it from the board, Reinforce it, Recall evacuates it Or do it all from the board: Attack on a system's row raises a fleet at your chosen colony, sized by the Fleet lever against the swarms seen there, carrying fuel and marines by the levers, and holds the system for the Days lever. It blockades, bombs while it has fuel, lands its marines on arrival and comes home when both are spent Its size on the board is what your last scout saw. Nothing about a hive is live
The Threat tab: the swarm's fronts on five human worlds, and every found system nearest first with the last scout's note.
A hive system under attack: its worlds bud fleets out of their strata.
Defending your worlds A colony's defence is its ground defences manned by marines, plus its spare marines armed with heavy armaments. No marines, no defence: a colony fights with what is in its stockpile Marines arm over days, take losses daily while a front stands, and gain veterancy. Heavy armaments are burned per marine per day The fight is one line. Each side pushes with its strength; the net moves the line; a district changes hands when it moves far enough. The board reads it from your side: gaining, grinding, losing Push spends cover to move the line; Hold regrows cover. A dug-in force breaks under enough weight; an outnumbered push still gains, slower Each district the swarm holds is an industry it is eating. Take the district back and the industry rebuilds from where it was. Finish eating and it is gone for good Every front row says what is next (Objective), when (ETA) and when it ends (Victory). Hover for the figures each side needs While the swarm holds the orbit the colony cannot dock anything; relief convoys wait at the jump point
A front on Haven: who holds what, what each side needs, what is next and when.
A colony under occupation: Farming and Mining being eaten, Ground Defenses rebuilding after its district was retaken.
Your war board Mobilise puts every colony of yours on War Footing: a market condition that demands hulls, marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies, so your industries bank them as the colony's stockpile. The stockpile is the reserve the board spends Domain table: one row a colony with its stockpile, its fleet on station and its status. Levers above it, one per good: None / Med / Max is nothing, half or all of what the colony can spare Deploy raises a fleet from a colony's hulls at the Fleet lever and sends it where you say. Transfer moves stock between your worlds by convoy. Recall brings a fleet home with what it carries. Attack (Threat tab) sends a fleet at a hive system Every fleet and convoy pays fuel for the passage and burns supplies while out. It turns home when supplies run out, and its row says why Call for aid on a world under attack: a toggle per good. Factions with a surplus post offers; Accept, Dismiss or Cancel. Their asks of you show the exact figure, the standing it pays and the ETA; Send or ignore Defend an ally's orbit for 30 / 90 / 180 days, or send any good to any faction; standing on arrival, one rate either way Outpost: dock at any uncolonised world to build one. Storage, refit, a base of your own Nothing of yours moves unless you order it. No order of yours is refused Every other mobilised faction has a tab: its worlds, fronts, fleets and requests, read the same way
Your tab: three factions answering Arkoman's call for marines, two fronts, and your Domain with its levers and orders.
The sector A faction mobilises when one of its worlds is struck, never before. Its colonies bank the same reserves yours do It attacks with one grand fleet: half its navy and every marine and fuel unit its bases can spare, to the nearest hive it outweighs. It bombs and lands until the hive is gone, moves to the next it can reach, and comes home when its holds run dry Factions aid each other through the same asks and offers you see, their own colonies first Every strike, grand fleet, convoy and scout is a real fleet you can meet, intercept or fight beside Kill every hive and every faction stands down
Fog of war No radar on either side. A hive is found when a ship sees it and gets home Patrols on both sides. One that cannot outrun a strike dies with its warning The board shows what your scouts reported and how old it is. The map veils what you have not found The swarm only strikes worlds its own scouts have charted
Start your way Default: a hive seeded on the fringe at game start, striking once it can pay Chill: wake it after the Abyssal questline, or when your colony reaches size 6 Instant War: a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle
The settings menu (LunaLib, Shift+F2) holds the knobs that matter; the rest live in [tt]data/config/settings.json[/tt].
Changelog
0.9.2 - swarm doctrine Spoiler Threat fleets fight by what they carry, and big swarms carry fabricators again. Saves from 0.9 carry on: fleets already flying get their fabricators on first load.
Battle doctrine by composition A Threat fleet with no fabricator or hive in the battle attacks as a swarm: every combat unit aggressive, never backing off, never pulling out to vent, on search and destroy. Before, such a fleet had no orders and ended every battle pinned on its own edge A fleet with a fabricator or hive deployed defends it, as vanilla Swarm Doctrine, Swarm Personality (aggressive or reckless), Swarm Never Vents and Swarm Engagement Range (LunaLib)
Fabricators A budded swarm (Defense and Shifting Swarms, occupation garrisons) carries one fabricator per 1,200 fleet points, at most 3, as its flagship. A fabricator is 600 FP of the fleet. A strike that musters such a swarm keeps its fabricator Fleets already flying trade their smallest plain Threat hulls for the fabricators their size earns, fleet points unchanged. Converted hulls, hives and overseers are never traded Fabricator Threshold (FP) and Fabricators Per Fleet (LunaLib)
Hive military options Raids and bombardment of a hive close only while the swarm holds its orbit, and the menu lists every fleet holding it, so Engage can always reach what closes them. A garrison from a neighbouring moon no longer closes bombardment while the menu says there are no nearby fleets

entry.title: The Abyssal War 0.7.0
entry.content:
The Abyssal War went from 0.6.1 to 0.7.0.
Human navies now open the war at full strength and win early ground victories. In testing they burned 10 hive worlds in the first two years, where before they burned one in five; the hive still grinds them down if the player stays out.
Hive fog of war A strike no longer reveals where it came from. The struck faction gets a lead and sends scouting parties to sweep the systems around it. Sieges, task forces and contracts act only on hives someone has found. The swarm scouts too: it only strikes worlds its Scouting Swarms have charted. Fleet archetypes: 12 new Threat variants, and strike, garrison, seeding and scout swarms are each built to their own shape. NPC navies Depots fill from the war's supply (importers used to bank nothing once mobilised) and start full the moment a faction mobilises. Sieges actually launch: staging bases bank toward the siege, and convoys carry full loads of marines, fuel and supplies. Sieges sail at full strength and weigh the Defense Swarms first. A base the swarms outweigh posts a swarm bounty, paid per Threat ship by hull size. Landings are sized to survive the hive's first counter-attack, with marines pooled from the faction's other bases. When the nearest base cannot pay for a siege, the next nearest sails instead. Hunting forces: a base with no siege of its own hunts a bountied hive's Defense Swarms. Fleets from every base in reach muster outside the system and go in as one fleet. Allies answer a siege call with a hunting force. Player Hunt replaces Intercept: send a task force to hunt a hive's Defense Swarms from the board. Your hunting fleets collect swarm bounties on their own. Raid the fortifications: a colony's Ground Defenses, Heavy Batteries, Patrol HQ, Military Base and High Command are on the Disrupt raid list at Heavy danger. Raids wear them down past the orbital floor, and every raid's days count in full. Committing many marines to one structure costs more against a strong garrison, so several shallow raids beat one deep one. Off with Nexerelin, whose own bombardment covers it. The war board lists only the hive systems you have found, and stays off the intel list until you find the first. Fixes Help requests now withdraw and expire; Defend windows close. Hive worlds no longer post survey, analyze or procurement missions. A hunting force that never fights gets its fuel and supplies back in full. A swarm out raiding or reinforcing keeps its slot at home, so garrisons no longer overshoot the cap. Hives no longer found colonies in inhabited core systems. NPC sieges bombard until their landing can survive the first counter-attack, and pool armaments as well as marines. Siege landings, NPC and yours, are sized for the defences orbit can actually wear down: a hive without batteries no longer gets a landing too small to hold. Hunting forces of hostile factions no longer meet at the same hive, and a force fights as one fleet (capped at 90 ships). Hunts no longer spend what a base has banked for its own siege. Your hunting fleets are no longer paid twice when you fight beside them; bounty standing comes once per battle. Hunt is no longer offered on convoys. Siege fleets no longer shuttle back and forth between worlds. The disabled Aid/Defend tooltip names the real requirement: a military structure and a Waystation. With LunaLib, the first launch moves Siege Max Fleets (10 to 25) and Mobilisation Stock (3 to 6) to the new defaults if they still hold the old ones; values you set yourself are kept.

entry.title: The Abyssal War 0.6.0
entry.content:
The Abyssal War went from 0.4.0 to 0.6.0.
Threat Incursion is now The Abyssal War. The mod id is unchanged, so existing saves keep working.
Ground war Eradication is a ground campaign, not a decline timer: land marines, take the strata, kill the Fabrication Core. Ground fronts push, dig in or withdraw; armaments burn per marine per day, so what a front carries is how long it lasts. Fronts push the moment troops land at holding strength; a dug-in front stays dug in until the next landing. Sieges fight for the orbit first. Bombardment wears fortification to a floor and no further - a front on the ground takes it the rest of the way. Threat strikes land fronts of their own on inhabited worlds, dig in, then make a final push. Colony defense is garrison troops times fortification, each worn down separately, with an orbital floor under the structures. Marines arm over weeks, take casualties, count toward counter-attacks, and carry veterancy both ways with your fleet's marine pool. Support and Defend fleet orders: hold the orbit, run the siege slice, or fight only while the front cannot hold. A Defend fleet at the orbital floor can break up its own hulls into troops for the front. Planetary shields buy real cover against orbital bombardment. The hive scours an unopposed enemy front after three days.
Strategy layer NPC factions enter war mode when the Threat strikes them; you mobilise or stand down yourself. Every colony banks a visible reserve of marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies. Convoys carry that stock physically - escort them, or let the swarm's raiders have them. Fleet orders from the board: guard, stage, intercept, support, defend, siege, recall. Guarding your own colony stages the fleet there: its strength counts at the host and folds into sorties. Faction view shows any mobilised faction's colonies, reserves and fleets, with a totals row and a colour key. Min / Med / Max load ladders on sieges, supply runs and convoy loads. Recalled and expired fleets sail home and return their surviving cargo. Sieges are leashed to the contested orbit; strays are recalled instead of chasing across the sector.
Player aid and outposts NPC factions are autonomous now: you aid them, you do not command them. Send Defend, Resupply, Reinforce or Strike from your own colonies, gated by a capacity ledger and reserve stock, earning standing on arrival. Factions post their needs as ordinary missions - deliver by colony fleet, or in person at the dock. Allies send each other aid by standing, without you. Build an outpost over any uncolonised world, or take one free by ground victory. Dock at it for storage, or decommission it. A later colony on that world inherits the outpost.
Economy War reserves are the colony's real resource stockpile, not a separate hidden ledger. Mobilised colonies carry the War Footing condition, so the war shows as genuine demand and a real shortage on the colony screen. Depots cover the colony's own shortages before they fund anything else. Convoys land as trade at the receiving colony. Bases need a Waystation; NPC mobilisation builds them.
Escalation Grudge and alarm: the swarm answers whoever hurts it most, and alarm speeds hive fabrication. A ground victory draws retaliation from the nearest hive. Coalition fleets answer a mobilised faction's call during a siege. Defense Swarms detach to raid convoys, then return to their garrison.
Board Ground Fronts table, per system, with order buttons on every front. Per-fleet rows with Recall and Intercept. Colony rows open vanilla's own colony screen. Purge commissions removed; sieges launch from the faction view. Tooltips rewritten: one line per fact, and every button says what pressing it does - or why it cannot be pressed. The intel list row reads at vanilla's own size now, next to Colony Crises.
Testing Instant War (LunaLib, Debug): stands up a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle.

Campaign Content Additions and Balance Changes -------------
- Overall Campaign Changes: ------------- - Revamped most new factions colonies to better follow industry count rules per colony size and size standards within vanilla factions. - Reworked mod economy to be more even in market share and resource spread between factions (in general) while hopefully still nurturing trade opportunities for the player through the simulation environment. -NEX Changes - Adjusted vanilla factions' starting relationships, diplomacy chance, and max relationships for all new factions. - Adjusted some extremes within new factions' starting relations and diplomacy chances. (Trying to stick to lore intentions here, but still learning Nex to a large degree. A first pass.) - Added base raiding behavior and increased invasion power of Adamantine Consortium. (should have no allies and needs this to remain a threat to the player/sector is the idea, but feedback welcome) - Removed pirate behavior features for Nex with Adamantine Consortium and reduced colonization chance overall. (Still happens occasionally)
--- Colony Changes: ------------- - Reduced Archean Order colony size for several colonies. - Removed Orbital Station from Xolydunne so it can be more easily raided. - Reduced the resource deposit quality for Ilyss and Arkmaros in some areas. - Reduced industry counts on many Adamantine Consortium colonies. - Added remote Luddic Church colony with refining, heavy industry and an additional military base with a large hazard rating. - Added two additional Sci-Corps colonies to better separate out industries and resources. - Removed Orbital Station from Yama and reduced the station at Nachiketa to an Orbital Station (down from a Battlestation). - Added Fuel Production and High Command to Gilead (based in the star fortress instead of the surface from a lore perspective) - Added Orbital Works to Tartesseus (again not on the surface- see above). - Increased size of Traveler's Triumph Station to 5 and added Heavy Industry. - Upgraded Traveler's Triumph Station to a Battlestation (up from an Orbital Station). - Removed Orbital Station from Salamanca to allow more raiding opportunities there. - Changed Kazeron's Military Base to a High Command. - Added a standard independent orbital station to Derinkuyu Mining Station to add to its defenses. - Removed patrol hq from Yesod and Ilm. - Changed ground defenses to heavy batteries on Yesod. Reduced heavy batteries to ground defenses on Mazalot.
--- Fleet Composition Changes: ------------- - Reduced number of dedicated carriers in Hegemony fleets. (partly for vanilla lore adherence and also to create more faction variety in battle tactics between factions)
-----
Combat Balance Changes ------------- - Reduced sustained DPS of Micro Repeater and Dual Micro Repeater. - Revamped ballistic weapon FX under these principles: - Yellow-Orange-Red color indication of assault-heavy assault-strike weaponry. - Bullet size now scales by tier to facilitate an intuitive learning of combat threats to armor and better teach a player when to raise shields. - Doubled cooldown of Phase Teleporter. - Added weapon slots and increased OP (if necessary) to most civillian ships to help prevent them from being overly vulnerable against fighters and missiles during retreat battles. - Added additional weapon slots and increased OP of some pirate and luddic conversion vessels (they are too weak). - Added a rear-facing small weapon to the Valkyrie and Valkyrie MkII to help give minor protection to its engines against interdiction-class missiles and upgraded the Valkyrie's central missile weapon size to medium to better combat fighters. - Added a built-in beam range increase to the Onslaught XIV hull to support it's built in foward weapons. (The AI uses them as a cost effective alternative more often now - even when equipping Devastators) - Added 3 additional small weapons (rear-facing) to Buffalo MkII and reworked variants for better synergy in attack builds. - Reduced per shot damage of Excaliber Cannon and Apocalypse Cannon line of weapons. Increased recharge/fire rate for those as well. - Made some ballistic weapons Energy damage instead of High Explosive damage. - Increased Revenant, Paragon and Megalith armor, max flux, and deployment cost. - Increased Megalith, and Revenant flux dissipation. - Slightly increased Megalith's base speed, removed all carrier limitations and benefits hullmods and replaced the built-in Accelerated Shields with a larger built-in increase to shield speed) - Increased armor and hullpoints for: - Pirate Atlas and Prometheus conversions - Rebalanced high tier vessel deployment costs. (FP cost slightly adjusted in a couple cases but mostly the same from before) - Increased speed of missile projectiles from bombers. - Increased attack range for missile projectile bombers. - Reduced hitpoints of missile projectiles changed above. - Reduced speed of phase orbs from Phantom bombers. Reduced their hit points. Doubled their turn rate. - Increased flight time of Hivemind orbs. - Combat Capacitors now allows the 0-flux speed boost up until 90% flux while active. - Buffed bomber defense across the board. Most heavy strike bombers release their payloads from further away. - Increased bomber damage. - Increased Claw bomber weapon armor penetration and reduced burst duration for more salvo accuracy. - Terminator Drones and Goliath Heavy Gunships will no longer target missiles or strike craft with their weapons and will instead focus upon their intended ship targets. - Obliterator and Heavy Obliterator no longer target fighters. entry.title: Starsector Language Pack - French 2.0.15
entry.content:
Starsector Language Pack - French went from v2.0.0-rc2 to 2.0.15.
This release fixes a critical incompatibility between the French Language Pack and Nexerelin.
Until now, players running the French Language Pack alongside Nexerelin (with its dependencies LazyLib and MagicLib) experienced two separate crashes: one when loading the game, and another when starting a new game, where the Nexerelin faction selection screen failed to appear. In practice, this made the French Language Pack unusable for a large portion of the community, since Nexerelin is one of the most widely installed mods for Starsector.
Both crashes are now fixed. The French Language Pack is fully compatible with Nexerelin: the game loads correctly, new games start as expected with the faction selection screen, and all French translations remain intact.
If you previously had to choose between the French Language Pack and Nexerelin, you no longer have to. We recommend updating to v2.0.15.
